newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sahnoun, Mbeki discuss Zaire talks venue.
newsitem.headline: Sahnoun, Mbeki discuss Zaire talks venue.

text.p: U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun had talks overnight with South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki about ways of starting Zairean peace talks, Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Friday.

President Nelson Mandela invited President Mobutu Sese Seko to attend talks in South Africa with rebel leader Laurent Kabila but Mobutu's son has said his father cannot travel that far due to ill health.
Sahnoun arrived back in South Africa on Thursday night from a visit to Angola and Namibia and spoke to Mbeki on the telephone, Pahad told state radio.
"We were exchanging notes about recent developments," he said. "We are trying to see what alternative venues are available...We have to find a venue that will allow President Mobutu to travel to it."
Pahad said both sides were still committed to meeting.

"We think it's more urgent now than at any other time to ensure the talks take place sooner rather than later...We will use our contacts with the international community to see if we can ensure these talks take place within days, rather than weeks," he said.
Pahad said Sahnoun's trip to Angola and Namibia had been aimed at putting pressure on the Zairean parties to meet for peace talks.
Kabila, whose forces control more than half of Zaire, has said talks with Mobutu must result in his agreement to step down and transfer power to the rebel alliance.
